liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **I Need A Miracle** (3 reviews): The transition from I Need A Miracle into Bertha is called the tastiest on record; Reviewer especially loves the Miracle to Bertha transition [14][15][16]
- **Eyes Of The World** (3 reviews): Weir outshines Garcia in this Eyes, though Garcia finds some new, interesting sounds near the end; With Keith Godchaux barely contributing, Weir steps out strongly with harmonic work alongside Garcia's rapid playing, making this Eyes noteworthy [5][6][12]
- **Peggy-O** (1 review): Peggy-O is praised as an all-time favorite with especially sweet playing [14]
- **Brown Eyed Women** (1 review): Brown Eyed Women into The Music Never Stopped is called very nice [11]
- **Estimated Prophet** (1 review): Estimated Prophet into Eyes of the World is singled out as a great pairing [9]
- **Shakedown Street** (1 review): Reviewer calls the post-Drums Shakedown Street one of the standout early versions [9]

## Setlist highlights

- **Ollin Arageed Jam**: rare: 3 archived performances [17]

## The recordings

- **gd78-12-17.sbd.wiley.13408.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 22 songs; 170 min; rated 3.83/5 by 6 [1]. Said about its sound: Soundboard of Eyes briefly drops to a muted, distant audience patch around the eight-minute mark, returning to soundboard by 8:21 [5]
- **gd1978-12-17.sony-ecm250.walker-scotton.miller.92528.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 23 songs; 178 min; rated 4.29/5 by 7 [2]
- **gd78-12-17.sony.wiley.9483.sbeoks.hnf**: audience recording; 22 songs; 159 min; rated 4.5/5 by 8 [3]. Said about its sound: Audience recording captures the timbre of the Grateful Dead experience; reviewer rates the sound highly; Audience recording has distinct high frequencies and crisp cymbals; called one of the best-sounding audience tapes on the archive; Audience tape's quality improves over time and is near-perfect by Shakedown Street; vocals sometimes get lost early [8][10][12]
- **gd1978-12-17.156927.aud.hicks-fong.flac1644**: audience recording; 22 songs; 162 min [4]

## Around the show

- The Fox is an old, historic movie theater with a balcony and a painted-cloud ceiling with twinkling star lights [11]
- Reviewer attended from the fourth row and has listened to the recording hundreds of times [14]
- Joani's recorder batteries died during Shakedown Street [2]
- Reviewer places this show within the mostly subpar late 1978 period, so expects nothing earth-shattering [6]
- First set is fairly routine, while the second set stands out much more [9]
- Reviewer considers 1978 one of the most underrated years, with Garcia especially on fire here [10]
- First half feels either a bit draggy or a bit rushed, but the band is at its best by Eyes [12]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd78-12-17.sbd.wiley.13408.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]
- **gd1978-12-17.sony-ecm250.walker-scotton.miller.92528.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Joani Walker; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Sony ECM-250 -> Cassette Master (Sony TC-158/Maxell UDXL-II90) D [2]. Also: Attendee met taper Joani, who made a cassette from her master and mailed it to him at UVa; Tapes came from Paul Scotton and Joani Walker; pitch correction was done with help from Joe B. Jones; The radio interview is a first-generation cassette copied from a reel master [2][15]
- **gd78-12-17.sony.wiley.9483.sbeoks.hnf**: source: Audience Recording: Sony 54P's [3]. Also: Attendee met taper Joani, who dubbed a cassette from her master and mailed it to him at UVa [16]
- **gd1978-12-17.156927.aud.hicks-fong.flac1644**: taped by concert recording by John Hicks & Dennis Fong.; transferred by Transferred by Andrew F. 05/2022; source: Handheld deck (mono) > MAC > 1st-Gen back-up tapes [4]. Also: Source was possibly a Panasonic portable, held up to head level by the taper, John; A mono-mixed patch from another source covers a tape flip in Drums, from 7:25 to 7:34 [4]
